notes.title: Update 17 (New game-mode: "King of the hill")
notes.content:
Added a "king of the hill" game mode this week, with a zero-g twist: the "hill" is an area in space that you have to float in. At the moment, the only map supporting this is "Chamber", as I designed it with this game mode in mind, among others. I'll probably find a way to add it to other maps in future too though, although it'll have to work a bit differently, since Chamber is the only map with a no-magnet zone so far. I've got a feeling someone actually suggested this game-mode back when ZGA was in greenlight, but I can't seem to find where, so let me know if that was you!

I've also rearranged the CTS_One map so that the team spawns are near the enemy's goal. This is due to a problem I and several other players noticed, where once a team got the advantage, it was virtually impossible for the other team to get the sphere back to the centre. With the team spawns near the enemy goal, as the enemy team brings the sphere closer to their goal, your team will spawn nearer to them, and get back in the fight quicker. This should produce closer matches. There's a risk that this will produce endless stalemates, but I'm hoping that will be mitigated by the addition of spawn timers. In any case, let me know how it goes if you get a chance to play on CTS_One.


ADDITIONS:
-New game mode: "King of the hill".
-New game mode: "Team king of the hill"

-Respawn timers. Each game mode has a different respawn time. No doubt I'll be tweaking them once I've tested these in-game.


CHANGES:
-Some pretty substantial changes to the CTS_One (the capture-the-sphere map).

-Now that there are game modes with various units for score (i.e. kills, goals, seconds), I've added the unit for the current game mode where the host sets a score limit, so they can make an informed decision.

-Also set a sensible max and min score limit for each game mode, along with a sensible default.


BUGFIXES:
-Fixed a bug whereby if you killed someone with the first shot after another player shot them, the other player would get the point. 
I've been aware of some kind of bug for weeks where I would sometimes fail to get a point after clearly killing another player (typically with the rail gun), and sometimes get a point for no obvious reason. I think this was probably the cause, so I'm particularly happy to see this one gone... if it really is gone, you never know...

notes.title: Update 16 (New map: "Chamber")
notes.content:
This new map has a couple of more experimental features. Most notably, it's main room has no magnet-floors whatsoever, and instead floating cover elements, which are positioned such that they can be swung between and around. I'll be very interested to see how this plays, and if it works well, then floor-less (pun intended) rooms are another map feature I'll be able to make use of in future.
The other experimental feature is less extreme, and more something I just don't happen to have done much of before, which is floors at 180 degrees to each other. There are two rooms dedicated to this concept in the new map. One of my concerns about this is that the transition between floors at 180 degrees to each other could be a bit disorienting/nauseating, when the camera flips around.

I have no idea how successful these new map features will be in practice, so do let me know what you think of the new map, and any observations you have on it.


ADDITIONS:
-New map: "Chamber"

CHANGES:
-The listen server host will now default to red team, for team game modes. This is because blue team has a slight advantage when the sides are uneven, since a new player will always be assigned to blue when joining a previously even game. I imagine that listen server hosts are more likely to be more experienced players, so it makes more sense to put them on the team with a slight disadvantage.

-I've made some changes to how the spawn location is chosen. I don't think you'll see much difference, so I mention this only because there's a higher than normal chance of spawning-related bugs.

notes.title: Update 15 (Minor weapon changes)
notes.content:
There's almost nothing that's completely new this week, I'm afraid, mainly changes to the weapon stats, as well as some fairly important bug fixes.
As expected, I don't think the rocket launcher is balanced very well, from my first guess at it's stats. My impression is that it's too hard to hit with. You might not get this impression always in free-for-all, since you can land opportunistic shots against people fighting each other and not paying attention to you, but what I found was that if you're trying to use it against someone who [i]is[/i] paying attention to you, it's virtually impossible to hit them.
I've also bumped up the damage a bit on the shotgun, SMG and laser, since a number of people have told me they think the time to kill is too long at the moment, and I feel inclined to agree. No doubt I'll tweak this more in future. The changes here are fairly subtle anyway, so quite probably the damage could stand to be even higher. 

ADDITIONS:
-Added a shock sound for the electricity room in "Core", and the CTS sphere.

CHANGES:

Rocket launcher changes:
-Increased blast radius to 2.5m from 2m
-Increased rocket launch speed to 12.5m/s from 10m/s
-Increased rocket acceleration to 10000m/s^2 from 6000m/s^2

Shotgun:
-Damage per pellet to 6 from 5

SMG:
-Damage to 15 from 14

Laser:
-Damage per second to 125 from 100 

BUGFIXES:
-Seems like I completely broke the homer gun when I was making the rocket launcher...somehow. It now homes again, but I had to guess at the original stats, so I don't know for sure if it's balanced the same now. That said, I think it was hardly balanced anyway.

-Pressing shift while entering text in the chatbox will no longer result in a kick.

-Fixed a bug where kicks would be registered against the place a player was standing before they died. Sounds bizarre, I know

-Fixed a bug where the electrical beams in "Core" would do too much damage to non-hosting players, generally killing on the first touch.

-I'm also pretty sure I've fixed the issue where the CTS sphere would damage a non-hosting player, then damage them again once they were clearly not touching it anymore. This issue was a bit random though, so I might just have not seen it since by chance.

-Also possibly fixed the issue where dead avatars go rigid and don't move. Pretty sure I've been under the impression that I've fixed this before though, so the same stands as with the above issue.

notes.title: Update 14 (Rocket Launcher)
notes.content:
The current weapon set has been long overdue improvement. Asides from the minor reworking of the laser and SMG a few weeks ago, most of the weapons have barely changed in over a year, since when I was prototyping ZGA. Anyway, it's got to the stage where I think working on the weapons is a high enough priority, so this week I've added a rocket launcher, into which I've put considerably more effort than I did with the old weapons. 
That said, I'll be amazed if the rocket launcher is anywhere close to balanced, since it's very difficult to estimate how easy it'll be to use on a moving target. Do let me know if you have any observations with regards to it's balance.

Anyway, one other, very minor, change I think I should draw attention to is that chat is now bound to T by default, instead of C. I don't think it'll change from C if you already installed the game though. I mention this because I can see it could cause confusion if existing players try to communicate outdated controls to new players.

ADDITIONS:
-Rocket Launcher! And about time too. It's available to pick up in all the maps with no Homer Gun and has replaced the Homer Gun in "CTS_One". With respect to tactics, I think it'll be very effective against targets on a floor, due to it's splash damage, but almost useless against floaty targets, due to it's slow projectile speed.

-The railgun has a new sound, courtesy of Deika. Deika's also given me some other sounds which I can use in ZGA, as soon as there are suitable weapons for them. So thanks very much Deika!

-Added a some text above the "start match" button to try and persuade server hosts to actually press it! If you were unaware, the server host is responsible for setting a score limit from the in-game menu, then pressing "start match" to remove the "game not in progress" warning.

CHANGES:
-The chat key is now T by default rather than C. I don't think this will change the keybinding if you already had the game downloaded though. You may wish to rebind it to T manually. In any case, be aware that this is the key new players will have for chat by default.

-Weapon symbols in the inventory HUD are now more transparent when the weapon is empty, to make it more obvious.

-Updated the brief game mode descriptions in the in-game menu. They referred to the advanced grapple control controls, which are no longer default.

BUGFIXES:
-Stopped multiple explosions spawning for the homer gun, on clients. The explosion that does spawn will quite often look way off from where the projectile is, if there was no lock on target, though. 

-Removed a possible cause of crashing. No idea how regularly this would have occurred for anyone, but hopefully that'll reduce the frequency of crashes for some.

-Fixed a bug where non-hosting players would not be throw back from the electrical beams in "Core" on contact. This generally resulted in more damage from the beams, since the character model remained touching them for longer.

-Fixed a bug where damage effects would spawn on teams in their own spawn rooms. No actual damage was applied though. I think I must have introduced this bug with the last update.

notes.title: Update 13 (New map: "Core" [featuring spherical floors])
notes.content:
Just a brief announcement first: I've recently learned that if you acquired ZGA while it was free, it will disappear from your library if you uninstall it. If you were hoping to hang on to it, I suggest you don't uninstall it! 


Anyway, there's a new map this week, with a pretty major new map feature: Spherical floors! From what testing I've been able to do so far, they work exactly as you'd expect. You can even go into orbit around them pretty easily, which is fun. How well they work in actual competitive gameplay remains to be seen, but if they work well then I'll be able to use them wherever I see fit in future maps.

As an afterthought, I believe someone asked me months ago if I could add walkable spheres, to which I said at the time I didn't think it would be possible in the scope of this game. Having thought about it at more length though, I came up with a pretty straightforward way to do it. I cannot for the life of me remember who it was that said that, but thanks for the suggestion!


ADDITIONS:
-Walkable spheres: These are pretty experimental, so you can probably expect there to be some technical issues, and probably gameplay issues too. Quite likely I'll have to make some adjustments in response to testing.

-New map: "Core". Features a large central sphere and other rooms branching off from the main room, including one with 3 smaller spheres in close proximity. I'm planning to iterate on this map somewhat after testing it. In particular I think it might need an extra room...


CHANGES:
-Decreased the mass of the CTS sphere. 

-The ammo bar is now below the health and defence bars


BUGFIXES:
-Realised I forgot to include the tutorial level for the mac version. Sorry about that, mac users! It's included now though.

-I noticed last week that if you die while kicking, the ragdoll adopts a straight legged pose, rather than flopping correctly. I'm 98% sure this is fixed now.

-There is another bug I've noticed that can happen on dying. It looks much the same as the one above, but I don't think it's related. The observable difference is that the avatar will not move or react to impacts in this second case, whereas it would in the first. Anyway, I'm much less sure about this one (since I have a less convincing theory as to it's cause), but I'm hoping it's fixed too.

notes.title: Update 12 (Melee kick)
notes.content:
Mainly a couple of important bugfixes, prior to the game's return to sale tommorow. There is a new melee kick though, which I hope people will find fun. Also, the shotgun should be more useable now.


ADDITIONS:
-A new melee kick attack. It's bound to shift by default. Does damage and knocks the target back in proportion to your speed. Probably a few will be aware that there was already a kick attack of sorts (I didn't include it in the tutorial because I was planning to replace it anyway), which just did damage when you "wall jumped" off a player. It was very tricky and confusing to use though. The new one should be much more transparent, in particular because the animation triggers irrespective of whether there is a player in range or not. In any case, the old one is still there (as something's got to happen when the wall jump hits another player anyway).

-Expanded the tutorial to include the melee kick. Also a few other minor changes to the tutorial


CHANGES:
-Shotgun now uses client-side hit detection, like the other weapons. This will remove any delay you would have experienced using the shotgun unless you were the server host. This is due to it being virtually unusable with a ping even somewhat high, due to the fast paced nature of the game.

-Put the weapons in the right order in the edit controls menu

-The framerate stat now updates every 0.3 seconds and shows to 0dp. This should make it much easier to read

-The magnetic fields in Pipe, Temple and Cityscape now extend to the ceilings.


BUGFIXES:
-Fixed a bug where your weapon would stop working if you tried to switch to the currently equipped weapon (by pressing the button twice, for example). It took me a while to figure out what was causing it, so I imagine most would have perceived this as weapons just stopping working randomly.

-There was an issue where, when adjacent to the ceiling and looking downwards (so that the camera was forced behind the ceiling), the grapple would attach to the ceiling, rather than the object visible thought the ceiling, causing you to get stuck. I'm pretty sure this should be fixed now.

notes.title: Update 11 (HUD, matchmaking, weapon changes + more)
notes.content:
There are a fair few significant improvements this time. Some of these things are pretty major components to what I wanted to get done prior to making the game available for download again. I'm currently thinking it shouldn't be too long now until it is. 

ADDITIONS:
-A brand new weapon HUD. Shows all owned weapons, with ammo. Is hidden by default and becomes visible when you switch weapon.

-Improved matchmaking:
	-You can now host password-protected sessions.
	-The game mode now shows in the server list
	-The map name now shows in the server list

-Your avatar's speed is now shown with ping and FPS when you press the h key. Added that for debugging and thought you might find it interesting. The units are cm/s.


CHANGES:
-The heavy laser is now replaced with what I'm currently calling the "Charge Laser". It is also the new default weapon. It's features:
	-Regenerating ammo (Regenerates at the same rate as it depletes, while not in use)
	-Fires while the mouse is held down, unlike the heavy laser
	-Is bound to the 1 key (default)

-The SMG that used to be the default weapon is now only pickupable in the maps. It has also had some changes. Overall it has been buffed slightly, now that it's not the default weapon. Changes:
	-Now fires at 12Hz instead of 20Hz
	-does double previous damage per shot
	-Has Several times the knockback intensity on the target, and increased recoil
	-Is now bound to the 4 key (default)

NOTE: Your old settings for weapon keys may be carried over. In this case, the laser will be bound to the "4" key and the SMG to the "1" key. I suggest you swap them yourself, so it matches the HUD. New players will have the correct controls by default though.

-Switching weapon during a weapon cooldown will now queue the action. This is also illustrated in the new weapon HUD.

-Various other changes to the HUD. Mainly making things less obtrusive.

Capture The Sphere:
-The sphere now does damage on contact and launches the contactee away. I think this might make for interesting gameplay, but also it's made the collision code for the sphere a lot simpler, which should solve various issues previously present, such as:
	-Avatar being pushed out of the map by the sphere
	-Sphere losing it's mind when someone enters walking mode while underneath it

-The ragdolls are now more flexible at the knees. Among other things, this has fixed the "crouch jump" bug. I think some of you may have believed this to be a feature, so apologies if you miss it. I can always add a deliberate one later.

-Improved lighting on the floors in most levels. Issue where adjacent floor sections were lit completely differently should be gone. Some pretty peculiar lighting in Cityscape now though, unfortunately.

-Possible performance improvements, as a result of the lighting changes. Seemed to observe pretty drastic improvements on my desktop, but little if any change on my macbook. Let me know if you see any improvements in performance or not.

-Hopefully the maps should no longer be excessively dark for those having that problem before. I believe it has so far been only with integrated graphics.

-Changed the colour of the lighting in some sections of "Factory" in a half hearted attempt to make it look more characterful. 

-Health and defence now are shown to 0 decimal places. I've no idea why I thought three were necessary before...


BUGFIXES:
-The landing sound previously did not drop off in volume with distance (same issue as with the weapons before). This should be fixed now.

-I've imposed a speed limit on the avatars of 100m/s. This should prevent the issue where you can slingshot yourself and others though the walls on Cityscape by reaching unreasonable speeds. It should also prevent similar issues. Nobody needs to go that fast anyway.

notes.title: Update 10 (Animation improvements to the transition between floating and walking)
notes.content:
This probably will seem like a pretty minor change to most, but for me, it's one of the most exciting changes so far. That is that I've finally found a way to smooth out the transition between ragdoll (floating) mode and the run animations. It doesn't necessarily look very natural yet, but I can probably improve on that in future. The important thing is that there's no "jumping" in the animation (so the character's limbs won't teleport to their positions in the run animation). I think that this kind of thing is very important to the "feel" of a game. Also, there will be minor gameplay implications in that it will be slightly easier to keep track of a target landing on a platform.

Anyway, that took most of the week, so there's very little else here, I'm afraid. There is a fix for one pretty major bug though, or I'd probably have left it longer before the next update.


CHANGES:
-Improved animation between floating and walking, as stated above

-Changed "Start new game" to "Start match" in the hope that this will make it's purpose clearer to the host.


BUGFIXES:
-Fixed a bug where you would lose control of your character if the host started the match while you were dead.

-Fixed hit marker not showing after melee kick that kills target

notes.title: Update 9 (New map: "Inception")
notes.content:
To make up for the lack of new content lately I've managed to release a new map. If you're wondering how I managed to do that in two days, it's actually an old map. The second map I ever made for the game, in fact, over a year ago I think. I've made some major improvements to it though, from what I've learned since then. 
Whether it's on par with the other maps, we'll have to see. There are still a few things about it that I've since decided to avoid doing. Also, it is a bit cramped, so I don't recommend you try it with very many players.

CHANGES:
-Re-arranged some of the magnetic fields on "Pipe", to try and reduce areas where they overlap (which invariably causes confusion).

-Fixed an issue where a shot that killed the target would not produce the hit marker

notes.title: Update 8 (Main menu and map improvements)
notes.content:
The main menu is now much more in line with what you'd expect from a finished game. It's not exactly pretty still, but is a good template for prettification.
Also, I finally got around to actually playing the game a bit last Sunday, which was enormously informative. As such, there are a lot of what I believe to be improvements to the maps, and various other balancing issues, particularly for Capture The Sphere.

ADDITIONS:
-An improved main menu. All the options from the in-game menu are now available from the main menu under "settings". Also, your graphics settings will now apply in the main and character edit menus, with the exception of FOV.

CHANGES:
-Development console now removed.

-While entering text in the chat box, pressing ESC or anything else that exits the chatbox, apart from Enter will now cancel the message instead of sending it.

-The next weapon and previous weapon controls (R and F by default) will now skip weapons with no ammo.

-The spawn rooms in capture the sphere now damage the opposing team, to prevent spawn-camping.

-The CTS sphere will now repel players with increased force on collision, while they're floating.

"Pipe" map:
-Removed the hidey-hole at the top of the shotgun room.

"Temple" map: 
-The ceiling now slopes downwards from the mountain to the arena. This is to prevent flying about the ceiling at such a distance, which I think was compromising the gameplay.

"Cityscape" map:
-Ceiling slopes now, like Temple, to prevent flying around at an unreasonable height.

"Factory" map:
-Added arrows underneath walkway in the room with the two sided section of walkway. This should make it easier to navigate.
-There's a new passage, from the room near the furnace to the bottom of the room with the double sided walkway. This is because it was too difficult to escape the area around the furnace, under fire. Also, it was just a bit linear.
-Other minor changes.

"CTS_One" map:
-Lots of changes, too many to reasonably list. This is in response to a series of games I played last week. Thanks to everyone who was involved in that, I plan to do more in future.

-Pressing the open menu key while it's open will now close it. Also, the movement keys now still work with the in-game menu open.

-The "return to main menu" button is now available to server hosts, but will provide 10 seconds warning to players as with "quit game".


BUGFIXES:
-The weapon sound spatialisation and drop off should finally work now. I thought I'd got this working before, but people were reporting the weapon sounds stopping intermittently. Turns out I'd forgotten to set the location of the sounds, so they were all playing at (0,0,0) {generally near the centre of the map}.


UNCONFIRMED BUGFIXES:
-Some people have noticed an issue where, upon being killed, your gun disappears, but you can still run about and cannot respawn e.t.c.
I believe these symptoms occur whenever the server thinks you're dead, but that message doesn't get to your computer, for whatever reason. Since all instances of this issue I've heard of were on a server with a noticeably poor connection in other respects, I expect this is either due to packet loss or UE4 deliberately not sending some data when the connection is congested.
I've made some changes that may or may not reduce the likelihood of this issue occurring. Let me know if you still see it happening. In any case, you ideally want to be on a server with a good connection.

notes.title: Update 7 (Tutorial)
notes.content:
To try and get to the root of all the crashes that seem to have appeared recently, I've put the game back in development mode. This won't have much a visible effect for players, for the most part. One noticeable effect though, is that you may have to re-enter your settings (graphics, input, character customisation). More details on this here: http://steamcommunity.com/app/467820/discussions/0/350540974002976744/

It's not impossible that putting the game back in development mode will actually stop the crashes from occurring, so if you were having regular crashes that stopped with this update, let me know.

Anyway, that's my main purpose in releasing this update, sorry for the lack of interesting or significant updates lately. One actual addition though this time is a very rough tutorial level.

Also, don't forget trying to join the server of someone on a different version of the game to you will fail and you'll be sent back to the main menu. You can't tell from the server list of course, but if that happens around an update, that's probably why.

ADDITIONS:
-A tutorial level. I'm not very happy with this tutorial yet, but I think it'll be better than nothing for the time being.

CHANGES:
-Character now takes 0.2 seconds to crouch, from 0.1.
-Game is back in development mode, from shipping, to make debugging easier for the purpose of addressing all the crashes that seem to have showed up lately.

notes.title: Update 6 (Simple/Advanced grapple control option)
notes.content:
I'm suddenly seeing a lot of reports of regular crashing. I imagine this was introduced with one of the last couple of updates, because I don't remember the game crashing regularly before then. Hopefully I'll be able to fix that fairly quickly, if people report the circumstances under which these crashes are occurring. One initial guess is that it might only be happening on the maps "Cityscape", "Temple" and "CTS_One". If you know otherwise, let me know, because I've had very little time for testing lately.

Anyway, really minor update this time, but there are a couple of things that I think were important enough to warrant releasing it anyway. One addition should make the grapple easier to use for new players. Also, I'm hoping the audio should be sorted out now.

Also, don't forget trying to join the server of someone on a different version of the game to you will fail and you'll be sent back to the main menu. You can't tell from the server list of course, but if that happens around an update, that's probably why.

ADDITIONS:
-By default, the grapple will now pull automatically, at maximum force. The old mouse wheel method can be re-enabled from the edit controls menu, or the in-game menu under the "mouse" tab. Thanks to Bandersnatch for this suggestion, which I believe will make the game much easier to understand.
The reason for this change is that in almost all cases, you'd want to set the grapple beam to maximum pull force immediately after launching it anyway. The main use for the "advanced grapple control" option though, is for swinging around objects, where being able to exactly control the grapple beam tension allows you to control the path of your swing. Swinging, I believe, is an under-used and important use for the grapple beam.
Note that the control method for the grapple beam that used the shift button is gone completely, as it was pretty redundant to have to press the shift button every time you launch the grapple when there's never a compelling reason not to. If you were using this method, you could rebind something else to shift now, if you wanted, although probably something else will be officially assigned to shift later.

-Put a couple of health boxes in CTS_One, just because I forgot to before.

BUGFIXES:
-It's been pointed out to me that I completely forgot to enable any volume drop off or spatialisation for any of the weapons. This should be fixed now, but it's difficult to test locally.

-I'm hoping you won't have to restart the game now, before joining another game, if the host crashed or something strange like that.

-Put a couple of health boxes in CTS_One, just because I forgot to before.

notes.title: Update 5 (Matchmaking improvements)
notes.content:
Note that it's more likely than usual that there will be new bugs with this update (see below), so if you encounter any, please let me know in the forums ASAP, and I may need to release a fix.
The good news is that I think I've finally got the player count showing in the menu for each server. This was far less straightforward than you'd probably imagine, so I'm not 100% confident in the accuracy of the method. If you have any reason to believe the player count is showing incorrectly, let me know. Note that it might just be that someone has joined or left the server since you last pressed the refresh button though. In any case, from testing so far, it seems to be accurate.
Also, I was going to try and add friends only servers, but that's also proving not entirely straightforward, so I've released the patch early with the player count stuff. I'm still hoping to be able to add friends only servers shortly, but in the meantime, note that now that you can set a player limit for your server, you can just set it to the number of people you wanted to play with and have them join quickly, which is better than nothing.

Finally, for those who have read the Early Access description, you will know that I was waiting to gauge the player response before committing to finishing the game. Although the response has always been positive, I was concerned that people were only approving of the game because it was free and goofy, but not because they thought it could ever have any value as a finished game that anyone would want to put any significant length of time into. Lately, though there's been a huge increase in the number of people who acknowledge the state of the game and specifically say that they look forward to the game being more complete (or something to that effect). This taken into account, I'm just about on the verge of committing 100% to finishing the game to the best of my ability. If you don't think the game will ever be worth actual money to anyone, I'd appreciate it if you let me know now, because if I commit to finishing it, the game must be monetised one way or another, although I plan to discuss this more with players before deciding on a monetisation model. 
Anyway, huge thanks to everyone who has provided feedback of any kind.

Oh, and one last thing, don't forget that you cannot play online with someone who has not got the latest update yet, if you have. You will instead be kicked to the main menu and probably have to restart the game. There's no way to tell from their server if they've got the update, but if you go and try and join a server soon after I release the update and the above happens, that's probably why.

ADDITIONS:
-The player count and player limit is visible for each server. This hopefully should also prevent an issue I believe was happening where joining a server could get you sent back to the main menu, if the server was full. This was just because previously, there was no way to check if a server was full or not. Now you will be prevented from joining full servers. I'm anticipating an issue where this could still happen if someone takes the last place on a server before you refresh the list, so if you try to join a server that's nearly full and get kicked to the main menu, that's probably what happened.

-When hosting a server, you can now set the player limit between 2 and 12.


CHANGES:
-Disabled the lens flair effect, because it reduces visibility.

-Players will now auto-join a team when joining a team game. They will be put in the team with fewer players, or blue team if equal. Note that you can still change teams however you want in between matches, so that you could do an asymmetrical game, if there is a large skill difference. This addition is in response to a report that some people don't seem to be joining teams...

-I've built the game in UE4's shipping mode, rather than development mode as in the past. This probably won't mean a lot to most of you, but here are all the noticeable implications I'm aware of:
	-The in-game console is gone. Hopefully you didn't know about it anyway.
	-Save files have changed location for Windows users. You will need to either re-enter 	 your previous settings or follow the instructions here: 	 	 	 	http://steamcommunity.com/app/467820/discussions/0/359547436757024927/
	 also, see the same discussion for more information.
	-Supposedly performance benefits. I highly doubt anyone will see a noticeable 	 	difference, but let me know if you do, because that would be nice to hear.
	-Fair probability of new bugs, as there always is with any significant change.
	-Log files have also moved to the same place as the save files. This is only relevant 	 if I've already asked you to send me some log files for debugging.

-Added a frame rate limit of 144Hz. There have been various issues in the past brought on by absurdly high frame rates, so I'd like to rule any more of them out. 144Hz is just the highest monitor refresh rate I'm aware of being commonly available. If you have a 145Hz monitor and feel discriminated against, just complain below and I can easily raise the limit.

-Set the default graphics settings much lower. Since these are only available in-game it's easier for someone with a beefy PC to turn them up than it is for someone with an awful PC to turn them down while running at 2FPS.


BUGFIXES:
-Fixed an issue where the game would prevent Steam voice chat from working by "using" the microphone. (Not extensively tested, please let me know if this persists)

-I've discovered I completely broke the Homer Gun with the last update. The projectiles would just pass through the target but it's fixed now.

	-Save files have changed location for Windows users. You will need to either re-enter 	 your previous settings or follow the instructions here: 	 	 	 	http://steamcommunity.com/app/467820/discussions/0/359547436757024927/
	 also, see the same discussion for more information.
	-Supposedly performance benefits. I highly doubt anyone will see a noticeable 	 	difference, but let me know if you do, because that would be nice to hear.
	-Fair probability of new bugs, as there always is with any significant change.
	-Log files have also moved to the same place as the save files. This is only relevant 	 if I've already asked you to send me some log files for debugging.

-Added a frame rate limit of 144Hz. There have been various issues in the past brought on by absurdly high frame rates, so I'd like to rule any more of them out. 144Hz is just the highest monitor refresh rate I'm aware of being commonly available. If you have a 145Hz monitor and feel discriminated against, just complain below and I can easily raise the limit.

-Set the default graphics settings much lower. Since these are only available in-game it's easier for someone with a beefy PC to turn them up than it is for someone with an awful PC to turn them down while running at 2FPS.


BUGFIXES:
-Fixed an issue where the game would prevent Steam voice chat from working by "using" the microphone. (Not extensively tested, please let me know if this persists)

-I've discovered I completely broke the Homer Gun with the last update. The projectiles would just pass through the target but it's fixed now.

tags.feature: -The player count and player limit is visible for each server. -When hosting a server, you can now set the player limit between 2 and 12.

tags.balance_change: -Disabled the lens flair effect, because it reduces visibility.

tags.feature: -Players will now auto-join a team when joining a team game. They will be put in the team with fewer players, or blue team if equal. notes.title: Update 4 (New game mode: "Capture The Sphere")
notes.content:
Many people have asked for a capture-the-flag style game mode, so I've tried to make something similar, that makes use of the game's core mechanics (in this case, mainly the grapple beam). Each team has to pull a large heavy sphere, using the grapple beam, to their respective goals in order to score points. You can also use the wall kick on the sphere to propel it (although, very slightly, because it really is rather heavy), but just barging into it will have no effect, unless you are the host (Due to complicated networking things that will likely need more work). 
This game mode is quite a complex addition, so it's highly likely there will be some undiscovered bugs for me to fix. Do please let me know if you encounter any. 
I'm also expecting this game mode will need changing a lot in response to play-testing, as well as the map, seeing as I couldn't rely on the same design principles as the other maps. 

Please let me know what you think of the game mode in the forums, as well as any issues you find, or ideas for improvements. An example of something that can be easily changed is the mass of the sphere, to make it easier or harder to pull.

Special thanks this week to RFz, who made the sphere model for the new game mode! If you're wondering why the sphere for "capture the sphere" looks better than anything else in the game, that's why. He also made the furnace mesh which is now making the Factory map look much more characterful.
Also, special thanks to "Dwarfz" for helping me brainstorm ideas for the CTS map. I generally struggle to pull ideas out of nowhere, so this sped the process up significantly, and most of his ideas have made it into the map.

Something to note is that the new game mode requires specially made maps. The only map for it now is the new one: "CTS_One".

Also, I forgot to mention last time, but trying to join the server of someone who doesn't have the update yet, when you do, will result in disconnection, so if that happens a lot around an update, that's probably why.

ADDITIONS:
-NEW GAME MODE: "Capture The Sphere". 

-Corresponding map for new game mode: CTS_One. Does not support any other game modes.

-The furnace type thing in the factory map now has an actual model, rather than just a glowing square. This model was also made by RFz. The furnace also now has some concavity, so is more dangerous to fall into.

CHANGES:
-I've increased the player limit for all maps to 12 from 8. The new game mode (and map), I think will be fine with that many players and Cityscape can probably support 12 players properly, but I do not actually recommend you play with that many players on any of the other maps. The game is untested for more than 8 players, so do let me know if you successfully do a game with more than 8 players.
[If you're wondering why I don't just set limits for individual maps it's just because of the dilemma of what to do if the host wants to change map to one that supports less players than are currently in the game. I don't want to stop them doing that while there are no private servers, as it could result in the host being unable to change map due to people joining (which is outside their control). This is hardly an unsolvable problem but, as ever, for the time being, a bit of organisation and cooperation is probably required for decent matches.]

-Doubled the impact force and recoil of the sniper gun.

-Doubled wall width on Cityscape "skybox" to reduce the chances of clipping through them for high speeds and low framerates.

-You will now teleport to a spawn point when the host starts the game

-I've increased the brightness of the fake stars on the "Temple" map. This is with the hope of making it easier to see players who are flying about the ceiling.

-Made grapple beam more glowy. It used to be more glowy and I can't remember why I made it less so.

-Weapons pickups are now ignored if your ammo for that weapon is full. This was mainly due to the addition of team modes, to avoid people picking up weapons they don't need that their teammates could use.

-This hopefully won't have a visible effect for anyone, but for my records: I've increased the client bandwidth cap from 80,000B/s to 160,000B/s.

-I've changed the method by which the in-game ping is acquired from the engine. Bafflingly, this seems to produce different values, for what is not really a complex measurement.

-You can now change team in between games

BUGFIXES:
-Fixed a bug where right mouse clicks weren't registered in the edit controls menu

notes.title: Update 3 (Minor fixes)
notes.content:
Once again releasing a more minor update sooner than planned. These are a few fixes for issues that probably would have been quite low priority if not for the recent surge in new players (I think due to the game being covered by a large YouTube channel). I'll probably make an announcement shortly explaining the current state of the game, and the immediate and long-term plans.
Anyway, the next update (unless I have to release another minor one first) should include a new game mode, with corresponding map. Hopefully within the next few days.

ADDITIONS:
-Added a brief explanation of the controls in the in-game menu.

CHANGES:
-Removed plain "Fullscreen" option, so only "Fullscreen Borderless" and "Windowed" modes are available. This is because I suspect the un-borderless fullscreen option was causing issues for some people.

-Removed view distance scale option. It didn't do anything anyway.

-Removed LAN mode options, since it appears LAN mode doesn't work.

-Grapple beam now no longer decays when grappling another player. Instead, it will break if it hits an intercepting object. This means you can now try to put an object between you and the grappler, if you are grappled. There is no longer a period where the grapple is unusable after it breaks though.

-You no longer have to press and hold the shift button again each time you launch the grapple. You can now just keep holding it, and the grapple will reel whenever you fire. Note that the press-and-hold control method is intended as an alternative to the mouse wheel method, rather than a distinct action. It is mainly for people without a mouse wheel, but you may prefer it anyway (I personally recommend the mouse wheel method, in which case, you could rebind shift to something more useful).

BUGFIXES:
-Health and defence now set to max on game start, as they are supposed to.

-Some users reported the game starting in VR mode when their VR device was plugged in (game does not support VR, problems ensued). Hopefully this is fixed now.

(Possible [untested] ) BUGFIXES:
-I've done something that I hope has fixed the issue where you had to restart the game between leaving one server and joining another. Do let me know if it's worked. I won't be unduly surprised if it hasn't though.

notes.title: Update 1
notes.content:
Was going to wait a bit longer and release a larger update, but one of these additions is so important that I've decided to release this smaller update early. The new feature I'm referring to is the notification of the host quitting. Previously, when the host of a listen server quit the game, everyone on their server would just be disconnected to the menu without warning, which could be very confusing, and quite probably mistaken for a bug.
Anyway, there's also another less critical new usability feature, which is the ability to view a list of players on the server. All the other changes and bugfixes are listed below.

I hope to release a more exciting update very soon, probably with a new map. If you've got any feedback on the current maps (what works, what doesn't e.t.c.), now would be a great time to leave it in the Feedback/Suggestions forum on the community hub.
 
ADDITIONS:
-You can now hold tab (by default) to show a list of all players on the server, including their score, and colour (so that you can identify them, or which team they're in)
-The host of a listen server quitting will now provide 10 seconds warning to other players (previously you'd just be disconnected without warning). Note that as host, you now have to wait 10 seconds before quitting too. Also, the host can no longer use the "return to main menu" button, only "Quit Game".

CHANGES:
-Grapple beam now deactivates on death
-Ragdolls now stay synchronised on death (Previously did not as a bandwidth optimisation)
-You can now change team before and after a match (previously were locked to a team as soon as you join)
-Made camera rotating to match floor smoother

BUGFIXES:
-Fixed hole in "Temple" map
-Fixed hit-marker showing when shooting corpses
-Fixed starting new game when dead causing loss of character input for listen server host
-Fixed team score HUD elements persisting after changing to free for all from team game modes. Still show personal score for team deathmatch, though, since this still makes sense.
-Reduced likelihood of a certain kind of disconnection issue (Reliable buffer overflow [don't ask]). I seem to be the only person who's noticed this anyway though.

-Fixed team score HUD elements persisting after changing to free for all from team game modes. Still show personal score for team deathmatch, though, since this still makes sense.
-Reduced likelihood of a certain kind of disconnection issue (Reliable buffer overflow [don't ask]). I seem to be the only person who's noticed this anyway though.

tags.feature: -The host of a listen server quitting will now provide 10 seconds warning to other players (previously you'd just be disconnected without warning). Note that as host, you now have to wait 10 seconds before quitting too. Also, the host can no longer use the "return to main menu" button, only "Quit Game".
-You can now hold tab (by default) to show a list of players on the server, including their score, and colour (so that you can identify them, or which team they're in)

tags.balance_change: -Grapple beam now deactivates on death

tags.feature: -Ragdolls now stay synchronised on death (Previously did not as a bandwidth optimisation)
-You can now change team before and after a match (previously were locked to a team as soon as you join)

tags.balance_change: -Made camera rotating to match floor smoother
